newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer in light volume.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer in light volume.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer, pushing through light resistance at 116.40 cents per lb in most-active July to begin revisiting recent highs as the market bounced back from its brief correction earlier in the week.

But dealers noted that most of Thursday's gains came during the last hour of trading amid light volume, involving local traders who bid the market up. Copper was still within its recent range, they said.
Most-active July COMEX copper settled up 1.35 cents at 117.00 cents, traded 117.20 to 115.60 cents. Spot June went out 1.15 cents higher at 116.75 cents.
International Copper Study Group said it expected a modest surplus in copper supplies this year following a roughly balanced market in 1996.
Dealers noted that LME stocks have begun a modest, rising trend, although it was not clear if this was an early sign of seasonal slowdown that traditionally takes place in the U.S. during the summer.
LME stocks rose 250 tonnes to 132,800 tonnes Thursday.
